public_rationale: The sources reviewed do not establish the operating profitability of OpenAI's product portfolio for the target period. Company-wide annual losses cannot settle that narrower claim. An independent estimate suggests positive API gross margins, but it covers only part of the business, excludes broader costs and remains unverified. Neither side meets the measurement requirements.
limitations: A broader reading that includes all company research spending asks a different financial question.
The period and cost allocation are evaluator interpretations because the sentence does not specify them.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's models and products are deeply unprofitable to operate.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI’s models and products — and we'll get into their utility in a bit — are deeply unprofitable to operate

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that operating the products collectively generated a substantial loss after attributable costs.
This does not require every product or every additional query to lose money.
Include serving costs and attributable staffing and maintenance costs. Do not automatically allocate all spending on future-model research to current products.

Because this is an ongoing observation without a completed period, use the first half of 2024, the latest completed half-year before publication. The surrounding full-year estimates are contextual projections, not realized first-half results.
Use estimate as the accounting basis because the surrounding financial argument relies on press estimates.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable first-half 2024 product revenue and attributable operating costs show a substantial aggregate operating loss.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable first-half 2024 revenue and attributable operating costs show that the product portfolio operated profitably or approximately broke even.
